explain.say: Did you know you talk to yourself all day long? Not out loud, but in your head! That inner voice is called self-talk. Look at the board: there are two kinds of voices.

faq.q: Why is my inner voice so mean?
faq.a: Often it is trying to protect you from mistakes, but it goes too far. It may also repeat unkind things you have heard. The good news is that you can train it to be kinder.
asks: Why do I put myself down?

faq.q: How do I change my self-talk?
faq.a: Catch it, check it, change it. Notice the unkind thought, ask if it is really true, then say what a kind friend or coach would say instead.
asks: How do I stop negative thoughts?

faq.a: Self-talk is the voice in your head that comments on what you do and how things are going. It can be kind and helpful, or harsh and unhelpful.
Yes, studies of athletes show that helpful self-talk, like "keep your eye on the ball" or "you can do this", can improve how well they perform.

faq.q: Is it weird to talk to myself?
faq.a: Not at all. Everyone talks to themselves, in their head or out loud. Talking yourself through a hard task can help you focus.

facts: A 2011 review of 32 studies found that self-talk helped athletes perform better in sport.
In a 2014 study, people who gave themselves a pep talk using their own name or "you" felt less nervous before giving a speech.
